subject.title: [Feature]: Add TTL/Expiry for Delivery Queue Messages

question: What outbound delivery expiry policy should OpenClaw expose for queued recovery: which config key, default behavior, and expired-entry action?
rationale: The missing source-level policy is clear, but adding a strict config surface and changing whether old queued messages replay after upgrade requires product and compatibility intent.

options.title: Opt-in messages.delivery TTL
options.body: Add optional messages.delivery.maxAgeMs with a failed or quarantine-style expired action, preserving the current no-TTL default while covering startup recovery and reconnect drains.

options.title: Finite Default TTL
options.body: Ship a default max age to prevent stale floods without user setup, accepting a compatibility-sensitive change to existing recovery behavior.

options.title: Broader Freshness Design
options.body: Pause the outbound-only fix and design outbound plus inbound stale-message policy together, reducing policy drift but delaying the known outbound repair.

recommendation.title: Opt-in messages.delivery TTL
recommendation.body: Add optional messages.delivery.maxAgeMs with a failed or quarantine-style expired action, preserving the current no-TTL default while covering startup recovery and reconnect drains.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of current delivery-queue history and prior issue-discussion direction for the config/default policy choice.
